(p-297) Surah "Al-Jathiyah" (The Kneeling)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Ha-Mim﴾. If you take it as the name of the surah, then it is in the nominative case as the subject (mubtada larger), and the predicate (khabar) is:

﴿The revelation of the Book is from God﴾, is a ṣila (a complement clause attached to a relative or a noun, here to tanzīl). If you take it as an enumeration of the letters (taʿdīd lil-ḥurūf), then "تَنْزِيلُ الكِتابِ" (tanzīl al-kitāb) is the mubtada' (subject), and the ẓarf (adverbial phrase) is the khabar (predicate).

﴿the Mighty﴾, in His retribution.

﴿the Wise﴾, in His management.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 45, verse 3:

﴿Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs﴾, that is, indications of His oneness. It is also possible that the meaning is: indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth are signs

﴿for the believers﴾. Its evidence is His saying:

**Verse 45:4 — Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil)**

﴿And in your creation﴾, and ﴿what He scatters of living creatures﴾ is conjoined to the noun in the genitive construction (al-khalq al-mudaf), because the noun it is attached to is an attached pronominal suffix in the genitive, and it is ugly to conjoin to it (i.e., to the suffix).

﴿Signs﴾: Hamza and Ali read it in the accusative (āyātan), while the others read it in the nominative (āyātun), like your saying: "Inna Zaydan fi al-dar wa-Amran fi al-suq" or "wa-Amrun fi al-suq" (Indeed Zayd is in the house and Amr [or: and Amr is] in the market).

﴿for a people who have certainty﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 45, verse 5:

﴿And the alternation of the night and the day, and what Allah sends down from the sky of provision﴾, i.e., rain, and it was named "provision" because it is the cause of provision,

﴿and by it He gives life to the earth after its death, and the turning of the winds﴾, "al-rīḥ" (the winds), read by Ḥamzah and ʿAlī,

﴿are signs for a people who use their reason﴾, with the accusative (āyātan), read by ʿAlī and Ḥamzah, while the others read it in the nominative (āyātun). This is an instance of coordination over two governing elements (al-ʿaṭf ʿalā ʿāmilayn), whether you read it in the accusative or the nominative. If you read it in the accusative, the two governing elements are "inna" and "fī," and the conjunction "wāw" takes their place, so it governs the genitive in "wa-ikhtilāfi al-layli wal-nahār" and the accusative in "āyātin." If you read it in the nominative, the two governing elements are the inceptive (al-ibtidāʾ) and "fī," and the conjunction "wāw" governs the nominative in "āyātun" and the genitive in "wa-ikhtilāfi." This is the view of al-Akhfash, because he permits coordination over two governing elements. As for Sībawayh, he does not permit it, and his explanation of the verse is that it is based on an implied "fī." What makes this acceptable in his view is the earlier mention of "fī" in the two verses preceding this one. It is supported by the reading of Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him: "wa-fī ikhtilāfi al-layli wal-nahār." It is also permissible for "āyātun" to be in the accusative as a specification (al-ikhtiṣāṣ) after the completion of the preceding genitive phrase, coordinated with what came before it, or by repetition (al-takrīr), as an emphasis of the first "āyāt," as if it were said: "āyātin, āyātin." Their nominative reading is by an implied "hiya" (it is). The meaning in placing faith (al-īmān) before certainty (al-iqān), and placing it in the middle, and delaying the other, is that the fair-minded among the servants, when they look at the heavens and the earth with sound observation, know that they are created, and that they must have a Creator, so they believe in Allah. When they look at the creation of themselves and their transition from one state to another, and at the creation of the various kinds of animals that appear upon the earth, their faith increases and they attain certainty. When they look at the other events that renew themselves at every moment, such as the alternation of night and day, the descent of rain, the life of the earth through it after its death, and the turning of the winds to the south and north, the east and the west, they understand, their knowledge is firmly established, and their certainty becomes pure.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 45, verse 6:

﴿Tilka﴾: a demonstrative referring to the verses mentioned earlier; i.e., "those [are] the verses,"

﴿āyātu Allāh﴾ ("the signs of God"). And His saying ﴿natluhā﴾ ("We recite them") is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: "recited,"

﴿ʿalayka bil-ḥaqq﴾ ("to you, in truth"). The governing element (al-ʿāmil) is what the word "tilka" indicates, namely the sense of pointing (al-ishāra),

﴿fa-bi-ayyi ḥadīthin baʿda Allāhi wa-āyātihi﴾ ("Then in what discourse after God and His signs"), i.e., after the signs of God, like the saying of people: "Zayd's generosity (karamuhu) impressed me," meaning "the generosity of Zayd impressed me,"

﴿yu'minūn﴾ ("believe"). The Ḥijāzī reciters, Abū ʿAmr, Sahl and Ḥafṣ read it with the letter tāʾ (tu'minūn), while others read it with yāʾ; the reading with tāʾ is on the assumption of the phrase: "Say, O Muḥammad..."

Woe to every sinful liar (every afak, a great liar),

sinful (one who is intensive in committing sins).

Note on the rendering: the Arabic terms "أفّاك" and "أثيم" are given in the English as they stand in the passage, with the glosses al-Nasafi supplies. The verse itself, ﴿Woe to every sinful liar﴾, is rendered as the verse's meaning.

(p. 299) ﴿who hears the verses of Allah﴾: in the place of a genitive (majrūr), it is a qualifying attribute (ṣifah).

﴿recited to him﴾: a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring back to "the verses of Allah."

﴿then persists﴾: he holds to his disbelief and remains upon it.

﴿arrogantly﴾: refusing to believe in the verses and to submit to the truth they speak, looking down on them and admiring what he has.

It is said: this was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, who used to buy tales of the non-Arabs (ʿajam) and occupy people with them instead of listening to the Qur'an. The verse is general, applying to everyone who opposes the religion of Allah.

The word ﴿thumma﴾ ("then") is used because persisting in error and being arrogant toward faith upon hearing the verses of the Qur'an is considered improbable to the intellect.

﴿as if he had not heard it﴾: the "ka'" here is the lightened form (mukhaffafah) of the particle "ka'anna," and the original is "ka'annahu lam yasma'hā," with the pronoun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-sha'n). The clause occupies a position in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: he becomes like one who did not hear.

﴿then give him tidings of a painful punishment﴾: inform him with news whose effect will appear on the skin.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 45, verse 9:

﴿And when he knows anything of Our verses﴾, that is, when something of Our verses reaches him and he knows that it is from them,

﴿he takes them﴾, that is, he takes the verses,

﴿in mockery﴾. He did not say "he takes it" (ittakhadhahu), to indicate that when he perceives any part of the speech to be among the verses, he plunges into mockery of all the verses, and does not restrict his mockery to what reached him. It is also permissible for the pronoun to refer to "shay'" (thing), because it carries the meaning of "al-ayah" (the verse), like the saying of Abu al-'Atahiyah:

"My soul is attached to something of this world; God and the Awaited Mahdi suffice it."

where he intended his reproach.

﴿Those﴾ is a reference to ﴿every sinful liar﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 26:222], because it includes the liars.

﴿For them is a humiliating punishment﴾, that is, one that disgraces.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 45, verse 10:

﴿Min warā'ihim﴾ (from behind them), i.e., min qudāmihim (from in front of them). Al-warā' (lit. "behind") is a name for the direction that a person hides from, either behind or in front.

﴿Jahannam. And what they earned will not avail them﴾, of wealth,

﴿anything﴾, against the punishment of Allah,

﴿nor what they took﴾, "mā" in both places is either a verbal noun (maṣdariyyah) or a relative pronoun (mawṣūlah),

﴿as protectors besides Allah﴾, i.e., the idols,

﴿and theirs is a great punishment﴾, in Jahannam.

(p-300) ﴿This is guidance﴾: a reference to the Qur'an. What indicates this is ﴿And those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord﴾, because the signs of their Lord are the Qur'an. That is: this Qur'an is perfect in guidance, just as you say, "Zayd is a man," meaning he is perfect in manhood.

﴿For them is a punishment of a painful kind (rijz)﴾: it is the most severe of punishments.

﴿Painful﴾ (alīm), with a nominative ending (raf'): Makki, Ya'qub, and Hafs read it this way, and it is an adjective of ʿadhāb (punishment). The others read it with a genitive ending (jarr), and it is an adjective of rijz.

Allah is the One who subjected the sea to you so that the ships may run upon it by His command (بِأمْرِهِ), that is, by His permission (بِإذْنِهِ),

and so that you may seek of His bounty (وَلِتَبْتَغُوا مِن فَضْلِهِ), by trade, or by diving for pearls and coral and extracting fresh flesh (i.e., fish),

and that perhaps you may be grateful (وَلَعَلَّكم تَشْكُرُونَ).

﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all of it﴾: it is a *ta'kid* (emphatic restatement, a repetition for emphasis) of "ما في السَماواتِ" (whatever is in the heavens), and it is the *maf'ul* (direct object) of "سَخَّرَ" (subjected). It was also said that "جَمِيعًا" (all of it) is in the accusative as a *hal* (circumstantial accusative, describing the state of the subject at the time of the action).

﴿from Him﴾ is a *hal*. That is, "He subjected these things, being from Him and obtained from His presence." Or it is the *khabar* (predicate) of an omitted *mubtada'* (subject), meaning "all these blessings are from Him." Or it is a *sifah* (qualifying adjective) of the *masdar* (verbal noun), meaning "a subjecting from Him."

﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 45, verse 14:

﴿Say to those who believe: forgive﴾ That is: "Say to them: Forgive, [and] they will forgive." So the thing said (the imperative "forgive" addressed to them) is omitted, because the answer indicates it. The meaning of "yaghfiru" (they forgive) is: they pardon and overlook. It has also been said that it is jussive by means of a hidden lam (the lam of command, "li-"), its underlying form being "li-yaghfiru" (let them forgive). Thus it is a new command, and the omission of the lam is permitted because it indicates the imperative.

﴿for those who do not hope for the days of Allah﴾: they do not expect the events of Allah against His enemies, from the saying of the Arabs about their battles: "the days of the Arabs" (ayyam al-'Arab). It has also been said: they do not look forward to the times which Allah (exalted is He) appointed for the reward of the believers, and in which He promised them success. It was said: this was revealed concerning 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) when a man of the polytheists, from the Banu Ghifar, insulted him, and he resolved to lay hands on him.

﴿That He may recompense﴾: this is a reason (ta'lil) for the command to forgive. That is: they were only commanded to forgive so that He may fully repay them for their forgiveness on the Day of Resurrection. The indefinite ﴿a people﴾ (qawman) is for their praise, as if it were said: "that He may recompense any people, and a people specifically distinguished by their patience over the harm of their enemies." "Li-najziya" (that We may recompense) is read by Ibn 'Amir (Shami), Hamza and 'Ali. "Li-yujza qawman" (that a people may be recompensed) is read by Yazid, meaning: "that good may be recompensed to a people," so the word "al-khayr" (good) is elided, since the context indicates it, just as "al-shams" (the sun) is elided in His saying: ﴿until it was hidden behind the veil﴾ [Sad: 32], because His saying ﴿when there were displayed before him at evening [the swift steeds]﴾ [Sad: 31] indicates the hiding of the sun. The estimated reading is not "that the recompense may be recompensed to a people," because a verbal noun (masdar) cannot stand in place of the subject, while there is a valid object present. As for making the second object stand in place of the subject, it is permissible, and you say: "May Allah reward you with good" (jazaka Allahu khayran).

﴿for what they used to earn﴾: of goodness.

Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own self; and whoever does evil, it is against it. That is: for it is the reward, and against it is the punishment.

Then to your Lord you will be returned. That is: to His recompense.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 45, verse 16:

﴿And We certainly gave the Children of Israel the Book﴾, meaning the Torah,

﴿and judgment﴾, meaning wisdom (ḥikmah), understanding (fiqh), or the settling of disputes between people, because kingship was among them,

﴿and prophethood﴾. He singled it out for mention because of the great number of prophets, peace be upon them, among them,

﴿and We provided for them of the good things﴾, meaning of the lawful and wholesome provisions that Allah permitted for them,

﴿and We preferred them over the worlds﴾, meaning over the worlds of their own time.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 45, verse 17:

﴿And We gave them clear proofs﴾, that is, signs and miracles,

﴿concerning the matter﴾, that is, concerning the matter of the religion,

﴿and they did not differ﴾, that is, disagreement did not arise among them regarding the religion,

﴿except after knowledge had come to them, out of rivalry among themselves﴾. That is: they did not differ except after there had come to them that which necessitates the removal of disagreement, namely knowledge. Their differing arose only from a transgression (baghy) that occurred among them, that is, from enmity and envy among them.

﴿Indeed your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ﴾. It has been said: what is meant is their disagreement concerning the commands and prohibitions of Allah in the Torah, out of envy, and out of seeking and acquiring leadership, not out of ignorance by which a person would be excused.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 45, verse 18:

﴿Then We placed you﴾, after the disagreement of the People of the Book,

﴿on a path﴾, on a way and a method,

﴿of the affair﴾, of the affair of religion,

﴿so follow it﴾, so follow your sharia (sharia, the revealed law), which is established by proofs and evidences,

﴿and do not follow (p-302) the desires of those who do not know﴾, and do not follow the desires of the ignorant, which have no proof behind them, and their religion, which is built upon whim and innovation (bid'a, innovation in religion). They were the chiefs of Quraysh, when they said: "Return to the religion of your fathers."

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 45, verse 19:**

﴿Indeed, they﴾, meaning: indeed, these disbelievers,

﴿will not avail you against Allah at all. And indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another, but Allah is the ally of the righteous.﴾ And they are his allies (those who take him as their protector). How clear is the difference between the two kinds of allegiance!

This is the Qur'an (al-Qur'an), the passage ﴿Hadha﴾ referring to the Qur'an.

﴿Hadha basa'ir lil-nas﴾ — He made what it contains of the landmarks of the religion (ma'alim al-din) and the sacred laws (shara'i') to be in the position of insights (basa'ir) in the hearts, just as it was made a spirit and a life.

﴿Wa huda﴾ — a guidance from error (dalalah).

﴿Wa rahmah﴾ — a mercy from punishment ('adhab).

﴿Li-qawmin yuqinun﴾ — for those who have certainty (yaqin) and are assured of the Resurrection (ba'th).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 45, verse 21:

﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think﴾, "Am" (or) is disjunctive (munqati'ah), and the meaning of the interrogative hamza in it is a denial of the supposing (inkar al-husban),

﴿that We shall make them﴾ "ijtarahu al-sayyi'at" means they earned (iktasabu) sins and disbelief. From this comes "al-jawarih" (the hunting animals/limbs, i.e., earners), and the saying "fulan jarihat ahlihi," meaning: their earner (kasibuhum),

﴿the equal of those who believed and did righteous deeds?﴾ "an naj'alahum" means "an nusayyirahum" (that We should make them). It is from "ja'ala," which is transitive to two objects. The first is the pronoun (hum), and the second is the kaf in ﴿kalladhina amanu wa 'amilu al-salihat﴾. The clause "sawa'un mahyahum wa mamatuhum" (their living and their dying are equal) is a substitute (badal) for the kaf, because a clause may occur as a second object, so it has the status of a single noun. "Sawa'an" (equal), read by 'Ali, Hamzah and Hafs in the accusative, is a circumstantial state (hal) of the pronoun in "najalhum." "Mahyahum wa mamatuhum" is raised (yartafi'u) by "sawa'un." Al-A'mash read "wa mamatahum" in the accusative, making "mahyahum wa mamatahum" two adverbs of time/place (zarfayn), like "maqdima al-hajj" (the arrival of the pilgrim), meaning: "equal in their living and in their dying." The meaning is a denial that the evildoers and the doers of good should be equal in life, and that they should be equal in death, because their states in life diverge: these lived in performing acts of obedience, and those in committing evil deeds; and in death, since these died with the good tidings of mercy and honour, and those in despair of mercy and in regret. It has also been said that the meaning is a denial that they should be equal in death as they were equal in life in provision and health. It is related from Tamim al-Dari, may Allah be pleased with him, that he was praying one night near the Maqam, and when he reached this verse he began to weep and kept repeating it until morning. It is also related from al-Fudayl that when he reached it, he began to repeat it and weep, saying: "O Fudayl, I wish I knew which of the two groups you are in!" (p-303)

﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, "bi'sa ma yaqdun" (how bad is what they decide) when they suppose that they are like the believers. For he who is seated on the carpet of conformity is not like he who is seated in the station of opposition. Rather, We distinguish between them, so We raise the believers and humble the disbelievers.

﴿And Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth﴾, so that it would serve as evidence of His power,

﴿and that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged﴾ is conjoined (ma'tuf) to this omitted, causal clause (al-mu'allal al-mahdhuf).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 45, verse 23:

﴿Have you seen him who has taken his own desire as his god?﴾ That is: he is compliant to the desire of the soul, following whatever it calls him to, so it is as if he worships it, just as a man worships his god.

﴿And Allah has led him astray knowingly﴾, from Him, by his choosing error; or He brought into being in him the act of going astray with knowledge from Him of that.

﴿And has sealed his hearing﴾, so he accepts no admonition,

﴿and his heart﴾, so he believes in no truth,

﴿and has placed over his sight a covering﴾, so he does not see a lesson. ("ghashwah" [read as ghashwatan], according to Hamzah and Ali.)

﴿Who then can guide him after Allah?﴾, after Allah has led him astray.

﴿Will you not then be mindful?﴾ With light stress (tukhfif), according to Hamzah, Ali and Hafs; and others read it with emphatic doubling (tashdid). The root of evil is following desire, and all good lies in opposing it. How well has one said:

Whenever the soul seeks you one day with desire, and there is a path for you to yield to it,
then leave it and oppose what you desire, for your desire is an enemy and opposition is a friend.

﴿And they say: "It is not but our life of this world"﴾, that is, "There is no life but this one," because they had been promised a second life.

﴿We die and we live﴾, in this worldly life in which we are. "We die," meaning we ourselves die, "and we live" through the survival of our children. Or some of us die and some of us live. Or we were dead, as sperm in the loins, and then we live after that. Or both states befall us, death and life. They mean life in this world and death after it, and there is no life beyond that. It has also been said that this is the speech of those who hold to *tanasukh* (transmigration of souls), that is, a man dies, then his soul is placed in a dead body and he lives through it. (p. 304)

﴿And nothing destroys us but time (al-dahr)﴾. They used to claim that the passing of days and nights is what causes the destruction of souls. They denied the Angel of Death and his taking of souls by the permission of God. They would attribute every event that occurs to *al-dahr* and *al-zaman* (time). Their poetry speaks plainly of complaints against time. From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Do not revile *al-dahr*, for God is *al-dahr*," meaning: for God is the One who brings about events, not time.

﴿They have no knowledge of that; they only conjecture﴾. They do not say this from knowledge or certainty, but from mere supposition and guesswork.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 45, verse 25:

﴿And when Our clear signs are recited to them﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, meaning what it contains of mention of the Resurrection,

﴿their argument is nothing but that they say: "Bring back our fathers, if you are truthful."﴾ He called their saying "an argument," although it was not an argument, because in their assumption it is an argument.

﴿Bring back our fathers﴾, i.e., bring them to life,

﴿if you are truthful﴾ in the claim of the Resurrection. "Their argument" is the predicate of "kāna" (was), and its subject is "an qālū" (that they said). The meaning is: "Their argument was nothing but their statement: 'Bring back our fathers.'" It is also read "ḥujjatuhum" with a nominative (ḍamma) ending, making it the subject of "kāna," and "an qālū" the predicate.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 45, verse 26:

﴿Say: "Allah gives you life,"﴾, in the world,

﴿then causes you to die,﴾ in it, at the end of your lifespans,

﴿then gathers you together for the Day of Resurrection﴾, that is: He will raise you all up on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever is able to do that is necessarily able to bring back your fathers,

﴿there is no doubt about it﴾, that is: about the gathering,

﴿but most people do not know﴾ the power of Allah over the resurrection, because of their turning away from reflecting on the signs.

﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And on the day the Hour is established, on that day the falsifiers will be lost.﴾ The governing element (ʿāmil) of the accusative case in "يَوْمَ تَقُومُ" is "يَخْسَرُ," and "يَوْمَئِذٍ" is a badal (substitution, a permutative apposition) of "يَوْمَ تَقُومُ."

﴿وَتَرى كُلَّ أُمَّةٍ جاثِيَةً﴾ ("And you will see every nation kneeling"), meaning sitting on their knees. It is said: "جَثا فُلانٌ، يَجْثُو" (*jathā fulānun, yajthū*), when someone sits on his knees. It was also said that "جاثِيَةً" (*jāthiyah*) means "gathered together."

﴿كُلَّ أُمَّةٍ﴾, with the *ḍammah* (رفع, *raf'*), as the subject of the sentence (*mubtada'*, the subject of a nominal sentence), and "كُلَّ" with the *fatḥah*, which is the reading of Ya'qub, as a substitution (*badal*, apposition) from "كُلَّ أُمَّةٍ."

﴿تُدْعى إلى كِتابِها﴾ ("is called to its book"), meaning to the pages of its deeds. He used the generic noun, so it is said: ﴿اليَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ ("Today you are recompensed for what you used to do") in the world.

(p-305)

This is the commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 45, verse 29:

﴿This is Our Book﴾. The Book is attributed to them because they are connected to it, since their deeds are recorded in it. It is attributed to God (Exalted) because He is its owner, and He commands His angels to write down the deeds of His servants in it.

﴿speaks against you﴾, that is, it bears witness against you for what you did.

﴿with truth﴾, without any addition or reduction.

﴿Indeed, We used to have copied down what you used to do﴾. That is, We had the angels record your deeds. It has been said that "nasakhtu" (I copied) and "istansakhtu" (I had it copied) have the same meaning, and that this does not mean transcription from a book; rather, its meaning is: We record.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 45, verse 30:

﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy﴾, that is, His Paradise,

﴿That is the clear triumph.﴾

﴿وَأمّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾, it will be said to them: ﴿أفَلَمْ تَكُنْ آياتِي تُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ ["Were not My verses recited to you?"]. The meaning is: "Did not My messengers come to you, and were My verses not recited to you?" The element to which something is conjoined (al-maʿṭūf ʿalayhi) has been omitted.

﴿فاسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ﴾ ["but you were arrogant"], regarding belief in them.

﴿وَكُنْتُمْ قَوْمًا مُجْرِمِينَ﴾ ["and you were a people of criminals"], i.e., disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 45, verse 32:

﴿And when it was said, "Indeed, the promise of Allah"﴾, referring to the recompense,

﴿"is true, and the Hour"﴾, read with the nominative (raf'), as a conjunction (atf) on the place (mahall) of "inna" and its noun, while "wal-sa'ata" (in the accusative) is read by Hamzah as a conjunction on "wa'd Allah",

﴿"there is no doubt about it." You said, "We do not know what the Hour is"﴾, meaning, "what thing the Hour is,"

﴿"We think only a conjecture"﴾. Its original form is "nazunnu zannan" (we conjecture a conjecture), and its meaning is the affirmation of conjecture alone. So the particle of negation and the exception were introduced, so that the affirmation of conjecture is conveyed together with the negation of anything other than it. The negation of what is other than conjecture was further emphasised by His words: ﴿"and we are not certain"﴾.

"And there will appear to them the evil deeds they committed," that is, the ugliness of their deeds, or the evil consequences (punishments) of their deeds, as in His saying: "And the recompense for an evil deed is an evil deed like it" [al-Shura: 40]. "And there will befall them that at which they used to mock," that is, there will descend upon them the requital for their mockery.

(p-306) ﴿And it will be said, "Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your day."﴾ That is: We will leave you in the punishment, just as you left the preparation for the meeting of this your day, which is obedience. The attribution of the meeting to the day is like the attribution of the plotting in His saying: ﴿Rather, it was the plotting of the night and the day﴾ [Saba: 33], meaning: you forgot the meeting of God (exalted be He) on this your day, and the meeting of His recompense.

﴿And your abode is the Fire﴾, that is, your place of settling.

﴿And you will have no helpers﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 25].

﴿That﴾ [i.e., the punishment],

﴿because﴾, meaning: because of the fact that

﴿you took the signs of God in mockery, and the life of this world deceived you. So today they shall not be brought out from it﴾, "لا يَخْرُجُونَ" (*lā yakhrujūna*, "they do not come out"), read by Ḥamzah and ʿAlī, [in place of the passive] "لا يُخْرَجُونَ" (*lā yukhrajūna*, "they are not brought out").

﴿And they will not be asked to appease [their Lord]﴾: it is not required of them that they seek to appease their Lord, i.e., that they satisfy Him.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 45, verse 36:

﴿So to Allah belongs all praise, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds﴾. That is: then praise Allah, who is your Lord and the Lord of everything in the heavens, the earth, and the worlds. For such all-encompassing lordship (rububiyyah) necessitates praise and commendation from every thing that is nurtured and sustained (marbub).

And to Him belongs the greatness (al-kibriya') in the heavens and the earth. ﴿And to Him belongs the majesty in the heavens and the earth﴾, and magnify Him: the traces of His majesty and His greatness have become manifest in the heavens and the earth,

﴿And He is the Mighty﴾, in His retribution,

﴿the Wise﴾, in His judgments.
